clarifications: Are intervals sorted initially? No, intervals are not sorted initially.
Can intervals be adjacent but not overlapping? Yes, adjacent intervals should not be merged.
What should be returned if there's only one interval? Return the interval itself.
Can intervals have negative values? Yes, intervals can have negative values.
Is the input modified in place? No, return a new list.
What if the input is empty? Return an empty list.
Are there duplicate intervals? Yes, duplicates are possible and should be merged.
expectedApproaches: Sort intervals by start time, then iterate and merge, O(n log n) time.
Use a stack to manage merging intervals, O(n log n) time due to sorting.
solutions: Sort the intervals by their start times. Initialize an empty list to hold merged intervals. Iterate through the sorted intervals, and for each interval, check if it overlaps with the last interval in the merged list. If it does, merge them by updating the end of the last interval in the merged list. If it doesn't, add the current interval to the merged list.
commonMistakes: Incorrectly merging adjacent but non-overlapping intervals.
Off-by-one error when updating the end of the merged interval.
edgeCases: all intervals with the same start
